body.x: CES 2025, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition, concluded in Las Vegas on January 10 (local time). The event featured the largest-ever "Seoul Pavilion," which made a notable impact at the global mega exhibition.

The Seoul Pavilion set up at Eureka Park—CES’s startup exhibition zone—spanned 1,040 square meters and hosted various participants. It was operated in collaboration with 16 organizations driving Seoul’s startup ecosystem, starting with its opening ceremony on January 7 and continuing for four days.

The pavilion was a joint effort of three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Gwanak, and Geumcheon), five startup support organizations (Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight major Seoul-based universities (Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kookmin University, Sogang University, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei University, Chung-Ang University, and Seoul National University).

The opening ceremony on January 7 featured representatives from the 16 participating organizations and 104 companies, alongside 103 supporters. They declared their vision for "Team Seoul" and announced their ambition to enter the global tech stage. Under the slogan “Team Seoul, ON BOARD to Dive In!” organization representatives participated in a symbolic “boarding ceremony,” with university supporters lighting up the ceremony with green aurora-colored glow sticks representing Seoul’s 2025 theme.

Seoul AI Hub, an institution dedicated to advancing AI-focused startups and ventures, joined CES 2025 with several innovative companies. Operated by a consortium including Seoul National University and the Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute (ETRI), Seoul AI Hub provides forward-looking office environments and business opportunities. Leveraging the technological resources and research capacities of Seoul National University and ETRI, the hub focuses on nurturing specialized AI talent and fostering innovative companies, aspiring to become a hub where people and opportunities converge.

Since its establishment, Seoul AI Hub has supported over 360 startups, including 100 resident companies and alums members, achieving cumulative sales of KRW 360 billion, investments of KRW 370 billion, and a combined corporate valuation exceeding KRW 1.5 trillion as of 2023. Seoul AI Hub strongly showed at CES 2025 to promote global market expansion for its resident companies. AVING News met with Chanjin Park to discuss their objectives and aspirations at this AI-themed CES.
Q. AVING News: This marks the fourth time Seoul AI Hub has participated in CES. How do you feel about this year’s event?

A. Chanjin Park: CES 2025, with AI as a central theme, features numerous domestic and international companies showcasing their promising and pioneering capabilities. Among the global startups at Eureka Park, the distinct presence of Korean companies is especially noticeable.

I take immense pride in participating in startups nurtured by Seoul AI Hub. Through our direct support, four companies joined the Seoul Pavilion, and 23 startups from our hub are showcasing their innovations through various channels at CES 2025.

body.x: Q. AVING News: Which companies from Seoul AI Hub are participating in CES 2025?

A. Chanjin Park: One notable company is Prevenotics Inc. (CEO Sooyoun Chang). They are presenting a solution that uses medical imaging data to detect cancers within the body, earning them an Innovation Award in the Human Security for All (HS4A) category.
Prevenotics stands out for its ability to track and manage early-stage or subtle precancerous lesions in the digestive system, offering a clear differentiation from other solutions.

Another remarkable company is StudioLab (CEO Sunghoon Kang), which combines AI and robotics technologies to create high-quality video and image content automatically. After winning Korea’s first Best Innovation Award in the AI category last year, StudioLab has achieved back-to-back Innovation Awards this year. Their GENCY PB solution is generating interest in the U.S., particularly in Hollywood’s massive content production industry, and they have connected with potential customers and partners during the exhibition.
Q. AVING News: What are your expectations for the opportunities created by CES 2025 for your resident startups?
A. Chanjin Park: CES 2025 presents an excellent opportunity for our startups to achieve tangible results. Seoul AI Hub is committed to supporting these outcomes.

While AI solutions saw rapid development last year, some investors and potential customers hesitated due to uncertainties about the technology’s maturity. However, AI technology has advanced significantly in just a year, gaining recognition as a viable solution in various industries.

As AI transformation continues to expand across sectors, I anticipate that global companies and investors will “Dive In” to the innovative technologies of our startups, aligning perfectly with CES 2025’s theme.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
